title: Harmonic Spectrum with G5/5 Limits (matplotlib)
description: The textbook G5/5 compliance figure: per-order bars, dashed planning-level limits, red bars where the harmonic exceeds limit. Pairs with the Harmonics lab CSV export.

blocks.text: Reads `harmonic-spectrum.csv` (Order, Magnitude_pct, G5_5_Limit_pct, Status). Produces the standard 'individual harmonic compliance' chart — orange dashes are the planning levels, bars turn red where they exceed.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('harmonic-spectrum.csv')
# Drop the fundamental and trailing summary rows
df = df[df['Order'].apply(lambda x: str(x).isdigit())].copy()
df['Order']           = df['Order'].astype(int)
df['Magnitude_pct']   = df['Magnitude_pct'].astype(float)
df['G5_5_Limit_pct']  = pd.to_numeric(df['G5_5_Limit_pct'], errors='coerce')
df = df[df['Order'] >= 2]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))

bar_colors = ['#ef4444' if (l == l) and m > l else '#2563eb'
              for m, l in zip(df['Magnitude_pct'], df['G5_5_Limit_pct'])]
ax.bar(df['Order'], df['Magnitude_pct'], color=bar_colors, edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.4)

# G5/5 planning limits (orange dashes, only where defined)
for _, row in df.dropna(subset=['G5_5_Limit_pct']).iterrows():
    ax.hlines(row['G5_5_Limit_pct'],
              row['Order'] - 0.45, row['Order'] + 0.45,
              colors='#f97316', linestyles='--', linewidth=1.5)

ax.set_xticks(df['Order'])
ax.set_xlabel('Harmonic order')
ax.set_ylabel('Magnitude (% of fundamental)')
ax.set_title('Voltage harmonic spectrum vs ENA G5/5 EHV planning levels')
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.25)
ax.margins(x=0.02)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('harmonic-spectrum.pdf')
plt.savefig('harmonic-spectrum.png', dpi=200)
plt.show()

G5/5 limits are different at LV, MV, HV, and EHV. The lab uses EHV values. Confirm which network voltage class your study applies to and substitute the correct table — incorrect limits can flip a 'pass' to a 'fail'.

For a multi-case figure (different operating points or with/without filter), use `subplots(nrows=2, sharex=True)` and call this routine once per axis. A 2×2 grid with shared x-axis comparing pre-filter vs post-filter is the standard 'effectiveness' figure.
